parts.note: not a ceremonial official but a plant: the spice mace grows on it, and a tree stands for a very long time

explanation.surface: A veteran official who carries the ceremonial mace.
explanation.walkthrough: Mace is a spice made from the husk around the nutmeg seed, so the 'bearer' is the tree that bears it; 'long-standing' fits anything that stands for decades.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropical evergreen that yields both nutmeg and the spice mace bears that spice and stands for many years.

parts.note: the first word in the old sense 'mean, tight-fisted' doubles as 'close by', and the people living right beside you are the lot at close quarters

explanation.surface: A miserly bunch crammed together in cramped lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near' is an old word for stingy, so the clue reads as a mean crowd, but it really means the people next door.
explanation.definitionFit: The people living right next door to you dwell at close quarters, and 'near' also once meant tight-fisted.

clue.text: Book he's found among a star collection

indicators.note: one piece is set among the letters of the other, so the first is placed within the second

parts.note: Taurus is a constellation, a collection of stars
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A man discovers a book in the middle of a group of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a star collection' suggests a gathering of celebrities, but it means a constellation of the zodiac; 'found among' places the pronoun inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A reference book listing synonyms is a familiar kind of book.

parts.note: E is a musical note
to have encountered someone is to have met them

explanation.surface: A creature spotted, a man bumped into, somewhere in a Cheshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in 12' points to NANTWICH, which holds ANT, and an emmet is a dialect word for an ant; those words just link.
explanation.definitionFit: An emmet is an old and dialect word for an ant, a small creature.

clue.text: … and one of his tropical country cousins

definitions.text: … and one of his tropical country cousins

parts.words: … and one of his tropical country cousins
parts.note: continues the previous clue's ant: a relative of that insect living in hot countries, often called a white ant

explanation.surface: A man's cousin from a hot faraway land, mentioned as an afterthought.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from the clue before, so 'his' is the emmet, the ant; its tropical 'cousin' is the white ant.
explanation.definitionFit: This wood-eating insect of hot climates is popularly called a white ant, a cousin of the common ant.

indicators.note: a development rearranges what was there, so these letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Where a new building project beside the river Thames is sited.
explanation.walkthrough: East Ham is a district of east London not far from the Thames, so the surface nearly describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: East Ham is a district of east London, so it is a place or location.

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so these letters are taken away from the bird

parts.note: a chicken is a bird
to ken is an old and Scots verb meaning to know

explanation.surface: A clever bird with a hunger for knowledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting to know' reads as curious, but 'wanting' means without and 'to know' is KEN, removed from the end of CHICKEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Chic means stylish or elegant, as smart does when said of clothes.

clue.text: An uplift for one in the crowd

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other, as one person stands within a crowd

parts.note: a host is a great crowd or multitude
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A boost for a single person standing in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoist is a lift upwards, an act of raising something.

clue.text: Took exception to some clumsy surgery

parts.words: Took exception to some clumsy surgery
parts.note: an idiom for getting angry, read literally as a body hacked about crudely by a surgeon

explanation.surface: A patient complained about a botched operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means to lose your temper; taken literally its words describe crude cutting by a surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn angry and quarrelsome is to take exception, and the idiom means exactly that.

clue.text: Always on the menu when Grieg fed out?

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The composer Grieg serving up a standard dish at a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Edvard Grieg was a Norwegian composer; the clue invites us to mix up his name with 'fed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fried egg is a staple of any breakfast menu, so it is always available.

parts.note: reads as a cheerful sailor, never stern-faced, but describes a nautical bearing at the ship's side, neither ahead nor astern

explanation.surface: A cheerful crew member who is never stern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' suggests beaming; read as A BEAM it is the nautical term for a position level with the middle of a ship, so not at the stern.
explanation.definitionFit: Abeam describes something at right angles to a ship's length, level with its middle, so away from the stern.

indicators.note: the exercise is placed inside the relaxation

parts.note: rest is relaxation
to train is to exercise

explanation.surface: A relaxation exercise that gives you self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control or the holding back of something.

clue.text: Worker in winch accident near Crewe

indicators.note: the worker goes inside the jumbled word
an accident wrecks things, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A labourer hurt in a winch accident near a railway town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accident' scrambles the machine word, and 'in' puts the insect inside it. Nantwich and Crewe are towns in Cheshire, England, so 'near Crewe' defines a place.
explanation.definitionFit: Nantwich is a market town a few miles from Crewe in Cheshire.

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so these letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Bad poets should be banned by law.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is a legal term for barring someone from asserting something, so to preclude by law.

parts.note: suggests a dispute with an accounts inspector, but an auditor here is a listener, and the trouble is pain in the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: A company having problems with its accounts inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks like an accountant but means a hearer; the trouble is an ache in the hearing organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain inside the organ a listener hears with is a trouble that afflicts anyone who hears.

clue.text: Yes men in the swim perhaps

explanation.surface: Flattering yes men keep up with the current fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Toadies who fawn over their bosses are sycophants, and swimmers doing front crawl are another kind.

clue.text: Notable teacher of some art design

indicators.note: a design is a new arrangement, so these letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: A celebrated tutor in some art and design subject.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a distinguished master or teacher, especially of music.

clue.text: Lachrymose source of grand tale translation

indicators.note: a translation changes the words, so these letters are rendered in another order

explanation.surface: A sad epic whose translation makes readers weep.
explanation.definitionFit: The gland beside the eye produces tears, so it is where weeping comes from.

clue.text: Their brutal methods take pages to compile

definitions.text: Their brutal methods take pages to compile

indicators.note: to compile is to put together, so these letters are assembled in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An account of a regime's cruelty would fill many pages.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the Nazi secret police's brutality would take pages to record.
explanation.definitionFit: The Nazi secret police were notorious for brutal methods, enough to fill pages of record.

parts.note: 'wicked' here means fitted with a wick, not evil, and the device gives light

explanation.surface: An evil scheme turns out to be enlightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' is read as having a wick; a device with a wick that gives light is a lamp burning oil.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamp burning paraffin through a wick is a wicked device giving light.

clue.text: Report of a revolution in the City

definitions.text: Report of a revolution in the City

parts.words: Report of a revolution in the City
parts.note: a report is a loud noise, and the City (London's financial district) had a sweeping upheaval in 1986

explanation.surface: News of a rebellion breaking out in the City.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district; its 1986 deregulation was nicknamed for a loud explosion, which 'Report' also means.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1986 deregulation of London's stock market was a sudden revolution in finance, and a loud report is a bang.

clue.text: A number in a French port couldn't be more game

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the port's name

parts.note: Brest is a port in Brittany
taken as written
V is the Roman numeral five, a number

explanation.surface: A count taken in a French harbour of the most daring.
explanation.walkthrough: AV goes after the B of BREST. 'Game' means plucky, so its most extreme form is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be game is to be plucky or brave, so being as game as possible is the superlative.

indicators.note: the town loses some letters, so they are taken away

parts.note: Basildon is a town in Essex
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A small-minded town in Essex sees a resident leave.
explanation.walkthrough: Basildon is a town in Essex, east of London. 'Simple' is not 'naive' but a noun: a medicinal herb.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple is an old word for a medicinal herb, and basil is a culinary and healing herb.

indicators.note: short of means lacking the end, so the final letter is cut off

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A composer who is going hungry.
explanation.walkthrough: Franz von Suppé was a 19th-century Austrian composer of light operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Suppé wrote light operas and overtures, such as 'Light Cavalry', so he was a composer.

indicators.note: to mess something up is to disorder it, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Svengali, the sinister hypnotist, abandons his mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Svengali is the hypnotist villain of du Maurier's novel 'Trilby'. 'left behind' is read as a noun phrase: what is left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Leavings are remnants, things that remain after the rest has gone.

indicators.note: the answer sits inside these words, running across the join

explanation.surface: A hearth in a Scottish town, let us suppose.
explanation.walkthrough: Stirling is a Scottish city, and the word itself is mainly Scots, so the surface fits.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingle is a fire on a hearth, or the fireside nook.

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means going upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: guns are arms, weapons

explanation.surface: Feeling at ease with one's hands in the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arms' looks like limbs but means weapons.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug means cosy and warm, so comfortable.

parts.note: a position in the old compositor's type tray holding the capital letters, with 'capitalise' meaning to set in capitals

explanation.surface: Printing firms take advantage of a business opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: Compositors kept capitals in the higher of two type trays; 'capitalise' means take advantage of, and also set in capitals.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital letters were kept in the top type tray, so its position gives the name for capitals.

explanation.surface: Asking for sugar, but only the tiniest bit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar comes in tiny particles of granulated crystal, and a speck is also the tiniest amount of anything.

parts.note: sounds like a robber's warning to a friend, but means the stalk that holds up a flower bud, and a verb to stop flow

explanation.surface: A gunman announcing a robbery to a pal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bud' looks like slang for a mate, but a plant's stalk holds up its bud; as a verb the word also means to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant's stalk holds a bud aloft, and to stem a flow is to check or hold it up.

parts.note: a breed with dark spots would like a pudding that shares its description, suet studded with currants

explanation.surface: Asking what a Dalmatian most likes to eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A British suet pudding studded with currants shares its name with a description of a Dalmatian.
explanation.definitionFit: This currant pudding is named like a Dalmatian, a canine covered in spots, so it suits that breed.
